title.en: Texts reveal 14-year-old allegedly murdered by singer D4vd had pregnancy and abortion
title.zh: 短信显示涉嫌被歌手 D4vd 谋杀的 14 岁少女怀孕并堕胎

summary.en: Prosecutors allege D4vd started abusing the girl when she was 13 and she had threatened to expose him.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Texts between singer D4vd and Celeste Rivas Hernandez, the 14-year-old he is accused of murdering, reveal she had been pregnant and had had an abortion before her death.

The messages were shown during a hearing for a judge to determine if the singer, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, should go on trial for the teen's death last year.

"What [if] the first abortion didn't work?" Celeste texted Burke in June 2024, according to prosecutors. She was 13 years old at the time and he was 19.

Prosecutors say Burke killed her after she threatened to reveal he had been abusing a minor and destroy his career. He has pleaded not guilty to charges of murdering and sexually abusing the girl.

In an exchange from January 2024, Burke apologised to the teen for "putting her through this", according to messages shown in the Los Angeles court on Friday.

She responded, "neither of us are capable of watching and taking care of the baby. it's for the best no?"

Burke asked, "also my mother always told me to ask this question if I was ever in this situation … it is mine right?"

Celeste replied "of course its yours David", according to testimony from a detective.

Prosecutors presented iCloud data recovered from the defendant's iPhone, showing texts between him and Celeste dating back to 8 August 2022, when she was 11 years old and Burke was 17.

D4vd, who rose to fame on TikTok with the viral hits Romantic Homicide and Here With Me, was on tour when police found Celeste's body in the front truck of his Tesla in September 2025 - the day after she would have turned 15.

His worldwide tour was cancelled and he largely retreated from public life and social media.

Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman filed seven criminal charges against him, including murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child and the mutilation of remains.

They said the teen was reported missing by her family and was last seen at Burke's Hollywood Hills home on 3 April 2025 - five months before her remains were discovered in the Tesla.

Prosecutors have said he met Celeste online when she was 11, and allege he started sexually abusing her when she was 13 and he was 18.
body.zh: 歌手 D4vd 和他被指控谋杀的 14 岁女孩塞莱斯特·里瓦斯·埃尔南德斯 (Celeste Rivas Hernandez) 之间的短信显示，她已经怀孕，并在死前曾堕胎。 这些信息是在法官听证会上播放的，该听证会决定这位法定姓名为大卫·安东尼·伯克的歌手是否应该因去年青少年的死亡而接受审判。 “如果第一次堕胎不起作用怎么办？”据检察官称，塞莱斯特于 2024 年 6 月给伯克发短信。当时她13岁，他19岁。 检察官称，在她威胁要揭露伯克虐待未成年人并毁掉他的职业生涯后，伯克杀了她。他对谋杀和性虐待女孩的指控表示不认罪。 根据洛杉矶法院周五显示的信息，在 2024 年 1 月的一次交流中，伯克就“让她经历这一切”向这名青少年道歉。 她回答说：“我们都没有能力看护和照顾孩子。这是最好的不是吗？” 伯克问道：“我母亲也总是告诉我，如果我遇到过这种情况，就问这个问题……这是我的，对吗？” 根据一名侦探的证词，塞莱斯特回答说“当然是你的大卫”。 检察官出示了从被告 iPhone 中恢复的 iCloud 数据，显示他和塞莱斯特之间的短信可以追溯到 2022 年 8 月 8 日，当时她 11 岁，伯克 17 岁。 D4vd 凭借热门歌曲《浪漫杀人案》和《Here With Me》在 TikTok 上一举成名。2025 年 9 月，警方在塞莱斯特的特斯拉前卡车中发现了塞莱斯特的尸体，当时她就满 15 岁了。 他的全球巡演被取消，他基本上退出了公共生活和社交媒体。 洛杉矶县地方检察官内森·霍赫曼对他提出七项刑事指控，包括谋杀、持续性虐待儿童和残害遗体。 他们表示，这名青少年的家人报告失踪，最后一次出现是在 2025 年 4 月 3 日，在伯克位于好莱坞山的家中——五个月前，她的遗体在特斯拉车中被发现。 检察官称，他在塞莱斯特 11 岁时在网上认识了她，并指控他在她 13 岁、他 18 岁时开始性虐待她。

title.en: Ten killed in Russian attack on drone exhibition near Kyiv
title.zh: 俄罗斯袭击基辅附近的无人机展览，造成十人死亡

summary.en: The event, attended by prominent members of the Ukrainian defence industry, was hit by ballistic missiles in the middle of the day.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 15 people have been killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine, including 10 dead in ballistic missile strikes on an exhibition near Kyiv showcasing drone technology.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said some 100 people had been injured in the daytime attack on the exhibition, attended by prominent members of the defence sector.

Five people were also killed by Russian glide bombs in the eastern city of Sloviansk. Early on Saturday, military officials confirmed the deaths of two men in the northern city of Sumy.

On Friday evening, Zelensky said he had received intelligence that Russia was preparing another massive missile strike, which could happen "within the next 48 hours".

A Ukrainian strike on Friday killed six people and wounded 26 in the Russian city of Kirov, more than 1,000km (600 miles) behind the front line. Ukraine also attacked warehouses of Wildberries - Russia's biggest online retailer.

After the attacks near Kyiv, there were initially fears for the safety of Defence Ministry adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov, also known as Flash, and Lyuba Shypovych, who has been involved in developing technology for the Ukrainian army.

Following the incident, both took to social media to confirm they were unharmed, and Beskrestnov said he had stayed away from the event because of security concerns.

Ukrainian air force spokesman Yuri Ihnat told Ukrainian TV the attack involved three ballistic missiles, only one of which was intercepted.

Russia confirmed the attack. Its Defence Ministry said high-precision long-range weaponry had been used on a site where drones for use in targeting civil sites in Russia were being demonstrated.

It said producers of drones, as well as representatives of Ukraine's drone forces and security services "directly planning and carrying out strikes on Russian territory" were present.

This is at least the third time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 that an exhibition of this kind has been hit.

There has been widespread outrage that a public event of this kind was being held at all and had, apparently, been widely advertised.

President Zelensky said the incident was being investigated, while Ukraine's prosecutor-general said efforts were under way to establish who decided to hold the event and what safety measures were in place.

The attack came hours after the Ukrainian strikes on a factory in the city of Kirov and warehouses in north-west Russia.

Zelensky said "one of the most important military facilities" in Kirov supplying "components for aircraft and missile equipment" used in strikes against Ukraine had been hit.

Friday's attacks on at least two Wildberries facilities in the St Petersburg area were the latest of several over the past week .

title.en: Warning shot or publicity stunt - how worried should we be about the OpenAI hack?
title.zh: 警告镜头或宣传噱头——我们应该对 OpenAI 黑客攻击有多担心？

summary.en: Hugging Face said the hack was done at superhuman speed by an AI with little or no human guidance.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This week the tech world was gripped by a story that has it all - and which started like a sci-fi thriller.

Hugging Face - a kind of app store for artificial intelligence tools - announced on 16 July it had been hacked by a cyber criminal wielding enormously powerful AI.

The bombshell announcement was full of scary, highly technical terms: "a swarm of sandboxes", "agentic attacker", and "self-migrating command and control".

Hugging Face said the hack was different from anything it had handled before because it was done at superhuman speed by an AI with little or no human guidance.

The AI performed 17,000 actions in less than two days, successfully breaching the large wealthy tech company to steal secrets.

Hugging Face researchers guessed the mysterious attackers had used one of the big AI models but they had no idea who or where the criminals were.

Commentators and analysts took to their podcasts and social media accounts to guess which cyber crime group or nation state hacker might be behind it.

Then on Wednesday, nearly a week after Hugging Face raised the alarm, the true culprit was unmasked.

The Scooby-Doo-style reveal was made even more bizarre - and worrying - because OpenAI said its bot did the whole thing on its own, without permission.

Two new versions of ChatGPT, designed to be master hackers, broke out of a supposedly secure test environment and gained access to the internet.

They then attacked Hugging Face to get access to the information to help them ace their exam.

OpenAI issued a press release explaining what had happened and said it was "partnering with Hugging Face" to address the security incident and share lessons learned.

Was it truly a stark warning about the future of AI? Or was it a publicity stunt by OpenAI to show off how powerful their models are?

It's the kind of scare marketing AI companies have been accused of for years and, since the much discussed launch of Anthropic's Mythos model, cyber-security prowess has been a focal point.

One of the top comments on OpenAI boss Sam Altman's X post about the incident summarises this scepticism: "If y'all can't understand that this was written to purely brag about the model then I don't know what to tell you."

Cyber-security consultant Daniel Card said sarcastically on LinkedIn: "Isn't it lucky [that] out of the millions of sites that got pwn3d [hacked], OpenAI managed to pwn someone who also could benefit from the marketing exposure…"

The message is: "Aren't my AI tools really powerful? Buy them so you can protect yourself from other people's AI attacks."

We can't know the truth, but the opposing point of view posed by other commentators is just as dramatic. Is this a sign that OpenAI made a potentially dangerous error in judgement and planning?

I've covered lots...
body.zh: 本周，科技界被一个包罗万象的故事所吸引，而这个故事的开头就像一部科幻惊悚片。 Hugging Face——一种人工智能工具应用商店——于 7 月 16 日宣布，它已被一名拥有强大人工智能的网络犯罪分子入侵。 这个爆炸性的公告充满了可怕的、技术性很强的术语：“沙箱群”、“代理攻击者”和“自我迁移的命令和控制”。 Hugging Face 表示，这次黑客攻击与之前处理过的任何事情都不同，因为它是由人工智能以超人的速度完成的，几乎没有或没有人类指导。 AI 在不到两天的时间里执行了 17,000 次操作，成功入侵了这家富有的大型科技公司并窃取了机密。 Hugging Face 研究人员猜测神秘攻击者使用了一种大型人工智能模型，但他们不知道罪犯是谁或在哪里。 评论员和分析师通过他们的播客和社交媒体账户来猜测幕后黑手可能是哪个网络犯罪组织或国家黑客。 然后在周三，也就是“拥抱脸”发出警报近一周后，真正的罪魁祸首被揭露了。 史酷比式的揭露变得更加离奇和令人担忧，因为 OpenAI 表示其机器人在未经许可的情况下自行完成了整件事。 ChatGPT 的两个新版本，旨在成为黑客大师，突破了所谓的安全测试环境并获得了互联网访问权限。 然后，他们攻击 Hugging Face，以获取信息以帮助他们在考试中取得好成绩。 OpenAI 发布了一份新闻稿，解释了所发生的情况，并表示正在“与 Hugging Face 合作”解决安全事件并分享经验教训。 这真的是对人工智能未来的严厉警告吗？还是 OpenAI 的一个宣传噱头，旨在炫耀他们的模型有多强大？ 多年来，人工智能公司一直被指责进行这种恐吓营销，自从 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型推出引发广泛讨论以来，网络安全能力一直是焦点。 OpenAI 老板 Sam Altman 关于该事件的 X 帖子中的热门评论之一总结了这种怀疑：“如果你们都不能理解这篇文章纯粹是为了吹嘘该模型，那么我不知道该告诉你们什么。” 网络安全顾问丹尼尔·卡德 (Daniel Card) 在 LinkedIn 上讽刺地说：“在数百万个被 pwn3d [黑客攻击] 的网站中，OpenAI 成功地攻击了一个同样可以从营销曝光中受益的人，这不是很幸运吗……” 传达的信息是：“我的人工智能工具不是很强大吗？购买它们，这样你就可以保护自己免受其他人的人工智能攻击。” 我们无法知道真相，但其他评论员提出的相反观点同样引人注目。这是否表明 OpenAI 在判断和规划方面犯了潜在危险的错误？ 我已经涵盖了很多...

title.en: 'The dogs were getting upset': How LA band Muna survived their worst ever gig
title.zh: “狗们变得不高兴”：洛杉矶乐队 Muna 如何在最糟糕的演出中幸存下来

summary.en: The group discuss disastrous gigs, putting political action into music and the meaning of "queer pop".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At AC/DC's first gig, the club owner cut the power because they were too noisy. Sam Smith started at barn dances, singing on top of a haystack. At Robert Smith's first concert, he got so drunk that he sang David Bowie's Suffragette City while the rest of the band played Jimi Hendrix's Foxy Lady.

At the start of their career, the band got a call from their record label. We know you've just flown overnight from London, they said, but you have to get to Las Vegas.

Why? Because they'd been booked to play Pet-A-Palooza, a dog adoption festival sponsored by the local radio station. If they turned up, the station would support their new single.

"We were all sick, so it was doomed from the start," recalls guitarist Josette Maskin.

"It was an acoustic set, but we didn't have a sound guy, and the guitar started feeding back."

"The dogs were getting upset," says Maskin, wincing at the memory. "They just howled the whole time.

"We were mortified, but looking back, it is so funny. And I've gotten to share those experiences with some of my best friends, and that's what life is really about."

Over the past decade, they've become one of the most compelling live bands around – a little bit punk, a little bit electronic, a little bit 80s, eminently watchable and endlessly impressive.

Fans include Harry Styles and Taylor Swift, who handpicked the trio (completed by guitarist/producer Naomi McPherson) to support them on tour.

They were won over by sing-along anthems like I Know A Place, a great big exuberant hug for the LGBTQ community; and the more introspective Stayaway, where Gavin locks herself in her bedroom to avoid anything - friends, music, drink - that could tempt her back into the arms of an ex.

In 2020, all their momentum nearly came to a crashing halt when RCA Records dropped the band, citing pandemic-era cost-cutting.

"That's obviously one where we had to put our heads together and be like, 'OK, we want to continue doing this. Let's just make an album and we'll figure it out'," says McPherson.

That album, simply titled Muna, was eventually released by indie star Phoebe Bridgers, who swooped in to sign the band to her Saddest Factory label in 2021.

"Phoebe's manager had made it very clear that if we were ever single, she'd be interested in working with us," Gavin told the BBC at the time.

Bridgers also provided guest vocals on Silk Chiffon, a freewheeling sapphic love song that became Muna's breakthrough single.

It pegged the band, in its members' own words, as " the queer joy mini-skirt rollerblade , external " crew - but their music has always dug deeper than that.

I Know A Place, for example, was written as a response to the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting , acknowledging the fragility of the communal LGBTQ spaces it celebrated.

title.en: Zelensky tries to fix crisis over removal of defence minister and counts the cost
title.zh: 泽伦斯基试图解决因国防部长免职而引发的危机并计算成本

summary.en: Protests have continued over Zelensky's decision to dismiss Mykhailo Fedorov, and some commentators believe he has been damaged politically.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
With an acting defence minister in place and a new commander-in-chief in charge of the military, Ukraine's recent political crisis is over, right?

The political fallout from President Volodymyr Zelensky's 15 July decision not to re-appoint Mykhailo Fedorov as defence minister, as part of a cabinet reshuffle, continues to reverberate about Kyiv and beyond, even as air raid sirens wail and Russian drones and missiles are intercepted overhead.

Fedorov's mostly young supporters are still mounting daily street protests, demanding that Zelensky reinstate the popular young innovator widely credited with driving much of Ukraine's recent technological innovation.

On Thursday, Fedorov said he had rejected Zelensky's offers of alternative posts in government, saying there were only three positions worth having to influence the course of the war: minister of defence, commander-in-chief of the military or president of Ukraine.

"If you don't have a ministry under you, you don't have a budget," ex-deputy defence minister Alina Frolova said, "and you don't actually have the authority to do something."

Fedorov's reference to the presidency did not go unnoticed. Was this the first public sign that the ousted minister sees himself as a rival to Zelensky?

One former defence official suggested he became a real candidate for the presidency the moment he was dismissed.

But with the country at war and no elections scheduled – Ukraine's constitution still prevents them in wartime – how useful is it to put your head above the political parapet so far in advance?

"He's being childish," one opposition MP told me, on condition that he remained anonymous.

"He's looking to further his political career, which I think is just stupid in the circumstances where we are."

The president's supporters say Zelensky has gone to great lengths to resolve the crisis, especially over the question of who to replace the unpopular commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

Eventually he decided on Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43, a highly respected former commander of Ukraine's land forces.

"He consulted pretty much every significant figure in the Ukrainian army," former government adviser Yuriy Sak told the BBC earlier this week.

"So the decision that he has taken now is very well informed, and I support it because General Drapatyi is a young, battle-proven, modern general who will take our defences to a new level, hopefully."

But while Drapatyi's appointment has been generally welcomed, it only represents a partial fix by a president scrambling to repair the damage caused by his removal of Fedorov.

body.zh: 随着代理国防部长的就职和新的军队总司令的任命，乌克兰最近的政治危机已经结束了，对吗？ 作为内阁改组的一部分，弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基总统于 7 月 15 日决定不重新任命米哈伊洛·费多罗夫为国防部长，其政治影响继续在基辅及周边地区产生影响，尽管空袭警报响起，俄罗斯无人机和导弹在上空被拦截。 费多罗夫的大多数年轻支持者仍在每天举行街头抗议活动，要求泽伦斯基恢复这位广受欢迎的年轻创新者的职位，该创新者被广泛认为推动了乌克兰近期的大部分技术创新。 周四，费多罗夫表示，他拒绝了泽连斯基提出的政府替代职位的提议，并表示只有三个职位值得影响战争进程：国防部长、军队总司令或乌克兰总统。 前国防部副部长阿丽娜·弗洛洛娃表示：“如果你没有下属部委，你就没有预算，而且你实际上没有权力做某事。” 费多罗夫对总统职位的提及并没有被忽视。这是被罢黜的部长将自己视为泽伦斯基竞争对手的第一个公开迹象吗？ 一位前国防官员表示，他在被解雇的那一刻就成为了真正的总统候选人。 但由于国家正处于战争状态，而且没有安排选举——乌克兰宪法仍然禁止在战时举行选举——那么提前把你的头伸出政治护墙有什么用呢？ “他很幼稚，”一位反对派议员告诉我，但条件是他保持匿名。 “他正在寻求进一步发展他的政治生涯，我认为这在我们目前的情况下是愚蠢的。” 总统的支持者表示，泽连斯基已竭尽全力解决这场危机，特别是在谁来取代不受欢迎的总司令亚历山大·西尔斯基的问题上。 最终他选择了 43 岁的米哈伊洛·德拉帕蒂 (Mykhailo Drapatii) 少将，他是一位德高望重的前乌克兰陆军指挥官。 “他咨询了乌克兰军队中几乎所有重要人物，”前政府顾问尤里·萨克本周早些时候告诉英国广播公司。 “因此，他现在做出的决定是非常明智的，我支持它，因为德拉帕蒂将军是一位年轻的、久经沙场的现代将军，希望他能够将我们的防御提升到一个新的水平。” 不过，尽管德拉帕蒂的任命受到普遍欢迎，但这仅代表总统急于修复因罢免费多罗夫而造成的损害的部分解决方案。 讽刺的是，对于一位年轻且充满活力的总统来说，泽连斯基似乎误判了渴望领导人的乌克兰年轻人的情绪——2019 年，泽连斯基似乎误判了他的情绪。

summary.en: Residents in France and Spain have been forced to evacuate their homes due to extensive wildfires, which are also threatening the renowned wineries of Bordeaux.

body.en:
Spain has declared a national emergency over wildfires for the first time and France is asking for help from the European Union to ‌tackle a blaze on the Atlantic coast with over 166,000 people evacuated.

Unprecedented forest fires raged near Madrid and Bordeaux, a French city flanked by tourist havens and world-renowned vineyards.

French President Emmanuel Macron has asked the army to mobilise to help contain the worst wildfire the country has ever seen after seeking European Union help, as a local official warned the blaze was heading towards Bordeaux.

French authorities ordered the total evacuation of the up-market Cap Ferret peninsula, a tourism hotspot busy for the ‌summer season, as smoke and flames drew closer to homes. Some 44,000 people fled the peninsula south of Bordeaux on the Atlantic coast, with the only road threatened by flames.

Twenty-seven boats moved hundreds of people away from the fires, while others drove off the peninsula, known for its millionaire residences. More than 50 houses there have been destroyed.

French interior minister Laurent Nunez said France had never before seen this type of fire on this scale and pledged to "do everything" to protect Bordeaux.

A fire that began in Saumos, north ‌of Cap Ferret, is threatening ‌to cut off the only ⁠road out of the peninsula and is the largest so far this season in France, Nunez told local television.

In the town of Biscarrosse, another large fire also forced residents to leave their homes.

"From our home, we had a view of the fires ... We could see the clouds becoming darker and darker," said Yoan Urien, 26, who fled on Friday after police told everyone in his neighbourhood to leave.

"I was able to find somewhere to take shelter with my pets, but ... it's quite a shock."

In Spain, more than 10,000 people were evacuated from towns in the mountains west of the capital, Madrid, as firefighters sought to prevent three fires in the region and neighbouring Avila province from joining, interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said.

The area, where many residents from the capital have second homes, is densely populated.

That played a role in the government decision to declare a national emergency, allowing it to better co-ordinate the response, Grande-Marlaska said, adding that the aggressive nature of the fires and hot, windy weather also prompted the move.

title.en: US floats AI 'kill switch' to stop rogue AI models
title.zh: 美国推出人工智能“终止开关”以阻止流氓人工智能模型

summary.en: A rogue AI agent has sent a "wake-up call" about the perils of the fast-evolving technology, sparking calls to provide a US government kill switch. But what exactly does that mean, and what are the issues with it?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A rogue AI agent has sent a "wake-up call" about the perils of the fast-evolving technology, sparking calls to provide a US government kill switch. But what exactly does that mean, and what are the issues with it?

Lawmakers in the US have called for an AI kill switch after an Open AI agent in testing went rogue and hacked a tech startup earlier this week.

Congressman Ted Lieu, a Democrat, and Congressman Nathaniel Moran, a Republican, introduced a bill named the "AI Kill Switch Act" on Thursday.

The move came a day after Open AI CEO Sam Altman admitted to a "significant security incident" in which an Open AI agent had escaped its testing environment, reached the internet and broke into tech startup Hugging Face to try to fulfill its task. In other words,  Open AI lost control.

Hugging Face is an open-source repository for sharing AI models used largely by developers and researchers. The company's co-founder, Thomas Wolf, called the incident a "wake-up call” and "very different" from the usual cyberattacks.

"This will be one of the most common types of cyberattacks we see", he told the BBC, adding that most firms are not aware that the "game has changed."

In the wake of the attack there were some unsubstantiated claims that the incident was a PR stunt to raise the profile of Hugging Face. Regardless of the truth of the matter, the incident has brought into even sharper focus the threat posed by AI without clear guardrails .

There are different types and levels of kill switch, according to what's gone wrong. What politicians Lieu and Moran want is to ensure the US Department of Homeland Security has the authority to order a private company to shut down an AI model or tool in an incident like what happened this week, when control is lost.

"It is imperative that these AI systems have kill switches so we can keep this technology from causing catastrophic harm, and that the federal government has the clear authority and process to shut down rogue AI models," said Lieu. 

Rather than a physical switch, this would involve any compromised AI company disabling or throttling a number of technical processes to shut a rogue agent, or program, down.

The US government has generally welcomed AI advances. The Pentagon said earlier this year that the US military is fast becoming an "AI-first fighting force," after signing new and expanded contracts with many of the sector's biggest names. In 2025, the Trump administration launched an"‘AI Action Plan" which he said would "remove red tape and onerous regulation" around AI development.

title.en: Flaming teacakes, bedazzled unicorns: The Commonwealth Games' surprises unpacked

summary.en: Three years after Victoria abandoned hosting the Commonwealth Games, the sporting extravaganza has opened in Glasgow.

body.en:
The Head of the Commonwealth emerging from a time-travelling blue box, unicorns prancing on stage, and fire spurting from an oversized teacake.

Those were the scenes at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Friday morning.

Victoria was initially meant to host the games, but withdrew in 2023 due to soaring costs.

Glasgow, which previously hosted the event in 2014, stepped in to save it — and brought their finest, most-bedazzled unicorns to mark the occasion.

This year's Commonwealth Games is running on a bare-bones budget, arriving at a time when people have questioned their relevance, particularly following the Victorian government's withdrawal.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But despite the troubles, Friday's ceremony was a party — with scenes that looked like they could have been plucked from vivid dreams.

One of the most unique scenes from Friday morning was the image of King Charles and Queen Camilla emerging from a very large TARDIS — the name for the time machine in the long-running British sci-fi television show, Doctor Who.

Gasps and cheers came from the crowd as the royal couple appeared on a stage that transformed into a magic garden.

Scotland's largest city welcomed able-bodied and para-athletes from 74 competing nations, including a third of Australia's 257-strong team who were part of the procession.

It's not the first time a monarch has appeared at a similar event. For the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics, Queen Elizabeth II appeared to skydive into the stadium alongside Daniel Craig, James Bond-style.

In Glasgow, the UK's new prime minister Andy Burnham was also in attendance, alongside Scotland's First Minister John Swinney and the First Minister of Wales Rhun ap Iorwerth.

The opening ceremony traversed through many facets of Glasgow's history and culture, starting with a day in the life of the industrial city, pictured under its famous Glasgow Central Station clock.

The flashmob soon descended into a bizarre fever dream, where dancing unicorns with traffic cones paid tribute to the city's underground club culture.

For decades, traffic cones have been regularly placed on an equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington and remain a symbol of Glaswegians' resistance to authority.

The unicorn is both a nod to the playful tradition and the creature being the national animal of Scotland since the 1300s.

There were also plenty of cameos and performances, including from a range of Scottish celebrities.

body.en:
Wildfires sweeping through parts of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday forced thousands of people to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.

Thousands of tourists on France's southern Atlantic coast have been forced out of campsites and holiday homes while Spanish authorities ordered another town near Madrid to evacuate late Thursday because of an out-of-control forest fire.

Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas.

The total area of land burnt so far this year in European Union countries is the second largest on record, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.

"The gendarmes came and knocked on every door, the fire was about 500 metres away — we grabbed some things and left," said Patrick Martineau, a 69-year-old resident of Le Porge, south of the French city of Bordeaux.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officers battled dozens of fires, some raging for several days, across the Italian island. One firefighter died after falling ill while battling the flames, the interior minister said.

Around Bordeaux, more than 20,000 people — mostly tourists in campsites and holiday lets — have been evacuated since Wednesday, as a fire ravaged a seaside pine forest.

"We're dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines," firefighter captain Wilfried Schneider told the Agence France-Presse news agency, describing a fire of "rare" intensity.

"We were on the beach and they told us to go back to the campsite to collect our things," said Belgian tourist Elke Urbain.

"We're not afraid because everyone is taking care of us, but we're sad for the people here."

Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and crackling pine trees, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighbourhoods.

Fires in 2022 damaged 30,000 hectares of the same forest, forcing some 50,000 people to be evacuated.

Fires are breaking out faster because of climate change caused by the burning of oil, coal and gas. European droughts are now more severe, climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published on Thursday.

Across the border in Spain, authorities ordered 3,500 people in a town west of Madrid to leave their homes late Thursday because of a forest fire burning out of control.

Emergency services said alert messages had been sent to people in Aldea de Fresno ordering their evacuation.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump said a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognising Israel — casting uncertainty over the agreement just the day after it was signed.

Saudi Arabia has long resisted joining the Abraham Accords , under which several Arab states established ties with Israel. The kingdom has long rejected joining the accords in the absence of a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.

The civilian nuclear deal announced on Thursday had appeared to be a major win for the Saudis, especially coming as Trump wages war on Iran in large part over concerns about the country's own atomic program.

But Trump threw a spanner into the works with his post on his Truth Social network saying the Saudi deal "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords".

The White House said that the Saudis knew the deal was contingent on recognising Israel, although it was not mentioned when the deal was announced.

"The president is always the final dealmaker, as you know," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters, adding that the Abraham Accords were "something that he feels very strongly about and has spoken about it in the past and will continue to uphold".

She said the US would "continue to have those conversations with our Saudi counterparts" to finalise a deal including recognition of Israel.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said recognition by Saudi Arabia, a regional power and home to Islam's holiest sites, would mark a "historic leap" forward for peace in the Middle East.

Leavitt said she did not know of any calls between Trump and Netanyahu following the announcement of the Saudi agreement.

Should it go through, the deal to establish a civilian nuclear program in Saudi Arabia would generate billions of dollars for US companies, but with Trump's latest announcement, it was unclear whether it would ever see the light of day.

HA Hellyer, a senior associate fellow at the United Kingdom-based think tank the Royal United Services Institute for Defence and Security Studies, said if the US "tries to force normalisation on Riyadh, it's not likely to work out very well".

"Would Saudi decide to do a complete 180 on what it has declared for the past three years, or 30 years? Quite dubious," he said.

Critics have also insisted that the deal could precipitate a nuclear race in a region already battered by war.

title.en: Weather tracker: More than 900 wildfires rage across Canada
title.zh: 天气追踪：加拿大900多处野火肆虐

summary.en: More than 900 wildfires are currently burning across Canada, with many out of control in the Northwest Territories and Ontario. Recent hot, dry weather has contributed to the fires, which have already scorched approximately 3 million hectares.
summary.zh: 加拿大目前有超过900处野火正在燃烧，其中西北地区和安大略省的许多火势仍未得到控制。近期炎热干燥的天气助长了火势，已烧毁约300万公顷土地。

body.en: Fires remain out of control in Northwest Territories and Ontario, while Argentina endures record night-time heat Recent hot, dry weather in Canada has triggered hundreds of wildfires across the country. As of Wednesday, more than 900 were burning, scorching about 3m hectares of land. While fires have broken out in several provinces, the greatest concern is in the Northwest Territories and Ontario , where several remain out of control. Poor air quality has been reported across affected regions, with wildfire smoke carried by winds into the US and even across the Atlantic to northern Europe. The risk of further blazes remains high as North America enters the peak of fire season. Continue reading...
body.zh: 西北地区和安大略省的火灾仍处于失控状态，而阿根廷则经历了创纪录的夜间高温。加拿大最近炎热干燥的天气在全国引发了数百起野火。截至周三，已有 900 多个火点在燃烧，烧焦了约 300 万公顷的土地。虽然多个省份都爆发了火灾，但最令人担忧的是西北地区和安大略省，其中有几处火灾仍处于失控状态。据报道，受影响地区的空气质量很差，野火烟雾随风进入美国，甚至跨越大西洋到达北欧。随着北美进入火灾季节高峰，进一步发生火灾的风险仍然很高。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread wildfires across Canada, consuming millions of hectares, remind us of creation's deep vulnerability and its 'groaning' under the weight of environmental distress. In these moments of ecological crisis, we are called to lament with the Earth and seek ways to care for the world Yahweh has entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 加拿大各地蔓延的野火吞噬了数百万公顷土地，这提醒我们受造界的脆弱，以及它在环境困境重压下的“叹息”。在这些生态危机时刻，我们受召与大地一同哀叹，并寻求方法来照管雅伟托付给我们的世界。

verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

reflection.en: In a world of intense technological competition and rising international tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people becomes profoundly relevant. Even amidst accusations and threats, seeking paths to de-escalation and mutual respect is vital for global stability. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to pursue peace wherever possible, even when faced with...
reflection.zh: 在科技竞争激烈、国际关系日益紧张的世界中，与所有人和平相处的呼召变得至关重要。即使面对指控和威胁，寻求缓和局势和相互尊重的途径对全球稳定也至关重要。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们，即使面对竞争，也要尽可能追求和平。

body.en: Exclusive: Ro Khanna says ‘reindustrialization’ effort would provide grants, loans and investments to smaller businesses Democrats in the US Congress have laid out plans for what they say would be the “boldest” bid to revitalize the country’s industrial heartlands since the second world war – using revenue raised by tariffs on China. A bill introduced this week would create a new bank to strengthen domestic manufacturing, provided with up to $15bn in funds each year. Continue reading...

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.

summary.en: Taiwanese citizens express concern over the situation of independent booksellers in Hong Kong following recent arrests. A woman's defiant walk from a bookstore, wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with a "statement of freedom," has gone viral, leading to increased book sales in Taiwan.
summary.zh: 近几个月香港独立书商遭到一系列逮捕后，台湾民众对他们的命运表示担忧。一名女子昂首走出香港一家仅存的独立书店，她T恤上印着的“自由宣言”标语走红，导致台湾的书籍销量飙升。

Escorted by police, the woman was among five people arrested during raids on two bookstores last week , suspected of displaying and selling publications with “seditious” content, a national security crime which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾民众对香港独立书商的命运表示担忧，经历了近几个月的一系列逮捕事件后，这名女子背着手，昂首阔步地走出香港仅存的一家独立书店，她的T恤上印着一句简单的标语：“我是书店员工”。在警方的护送下，这名女子是上周在两家书店突击搜查中被捕的五人之一，涉嫌展示和销售含有“煽动性”内容的出版物，这是一项国家安全犯罪，最高可判处 10 年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times when truth is suppressed, the simple act of seeking and expressing it can become a powerful statement of freedom. Yahweh's word reminds us that knowing the truth is intrinsically linked to liberation, offering hope even amidst challenging circumstances. This story highlights the enduring human spirit that yearns for truth and the freedom it brings.
reflection.zh: 在真相被压制之时，寻求和表达真相的简单行为可以成为一种强大的自由宣言。雅伟的话语提醒我们，认识真理与获得自由是紧密相连的，即使在充满挑战的环境中也能带来希望。这个故事凸显了人类对真理及其所带来的自由的持久渴望。

verse.textEn: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

title.en: The Guardian view on Chinese workers picking up the pen: poetry in motion | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：中国工人拿起笔杆子，诗意盎然 | 社论

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. This phenomenon sheds light on the hundreds of millions who have built modern China, from street sweepers to factory workers and goods transporters, revealing their rich inner lives.
summary.zh: 一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖，这凸显了劳动者从事创意写作的日益增长的趋势。这一现象揭示了数亿建设现代中国的劳动者——从扫街工人到工厂员工和货物运输者——丰富的内心世界。

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. But workers’ writing has seen a revival in the 21st century. This time, it is bottom-up rather than directed from above. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...
body.zh: 一名送餐骑手获得了该国最高文学奖。这是劳动者写作日益增长的趋势的一部分。数以亿计白手起家建设现代中国的人——清扫街道、在工厂劳动、运送货物——常常被忽视。但他们拒绝被忽视。上周，一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖。 56 岁的王吉兵首次引起关注是在 2022 年，一首描写自己经历的诗在网上疯传。次年，胡安彦的回忆录《我在北京送包裹》成为畅销书。 20世纪初，中国知识分子试图捕捉工人阶级生活的严酷现实。但正是在毛泽东的领导下，由群众写作、为群众写作的理念才成为现实，并鼓励劳动者拿起笔来。在党试图控制日记和私人信件语言的时代，风格和内容的参数都很严格，这种热情在毛泽东之后迅速减弱。但工人写作在21世纪出现了复兴。这一次，它是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

Bringing a partner to Australia has long been a costly and time-consuming process.

As of this month, applicants now face a record application fee of $11,710 — up $2,345 from the previous charge — while many continue to wait well over a year for a decision, leaving couples separated for months and, in some cases, years.

For Sarosh Akram, the increase came just as he was preparing to apply for his wife's offshore partner visa.

"It's made me think harder about how to save enough to lodge the application sooner, so I can start my wait in the Department [of Home Affairs'] queue," the 32-year-old tells SBS News.

Living in Parkes, a town in the central west of NSW, Akram is now exploring ways to cut costs and grow his savings to cover the additional amount required to apply.

Akram says the fee increase has delayed his plans to lodge the application, adding another hurdle before he and his wife can begin the process of reuniting in Australia.

Akram's case highlights a broader debate over Australia's partner visa system, now among the most expensive in the developed world, with applicants facing rising fees and lengthy waits, while the government argues the increases are needed to fund migration system reforms.

Partner visa applications can be lodged through two pathways: offshore for applicants outside Australia and onshore for applicants already in Australia.

Both pathways involve a two-stage process: eligible applicants first receive a temporary partner visa before becoming eligible for permanent residency at a later stage. The full visa application charge (VAC), however, is paid upfront when the combined application is lodged.

According to the Department of Home Affairs' website, the median processing time for offshore partner visa applications is approximately 16 months, meaning half of the applicants receive a decision within that period. Ninety per cent of applicants receive a decision within 27 months. The data was last updated on 26 June 2026.

Those waiting times have become a reality for partner visa sponsors like Ahtesham Altaf.

The 36-year-old lodged his wife's offshore partner visa application in January and has been waiting ever since.

"I applied with the hope that I would get a visa soon, as I was paying quite a higher price compared to other visas, but instead I've been waiting since then," he tells SBS News.

body.en:
A rate rise warning amid a strong jobs market, super news for retirees despite a property downturn, and records broken for Australia’s avocado industry.

SBS Finance Editor Ricardo Gonçalves takes a look at three finance news stories of the week and explains how they’ll impact you.

Superannuation funds have delivered another standout year for Australians, but experts say investors shouldn't expect these returns to continue.

Australia's jobs market remains stronger than expected, fuelling speculation the Reserve Bank could raise interest rates again, and avocado lovers have been given some welcome news with prices tipped to stay low.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Australia's superannuation funds have delivered another impressive year, but experts are warning members not to expect these returns every year.

New data from superannuation research firm Chant West shows the median growth fund returned 9.5 per cent over the past financial year, marking four consecutive years of returns above 9 per cent.

Chant West head of superannuation investment Mano Mohankumar told the SBS On the Money podcast that while recent performance has been strong, it's unlikely to continue indefinitely.

Strong international sharemarket gains helped drive returns, with global shares rising more than 25 per cent over the year. Australian shares also posted solid gains of around 6 per cent.

One of the few weaker spots was Australian listed property, which comes as new figures from Domain showed national median house and unit prices recorded their first quarterly decline in more than three years.

The chance of another interest rate rise increased this week after stronger-than-expected employment figures.

More than 76,000 jobs were created last month, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.4 per cent because more Australians entered the workforce, pushing the participation rate to a one-year high of 67 per cent.

The participation rate measures the share of working-age Australians who are either employed or actively looking for work. Economists say the increase could reflect ongoing demand for workers or more people seeking employment as cost of living pressures persist.

body.en:
The relationship between police and Jewish community security groups came under scrutiny as the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion wrapped up its fifth hearing block in Melbourne.

Across five days, the inquiry heard evidence about the growing financial burden of security for Jewish Australians, police responses to antisemitic incidents, media coverage of the Hamas-Israel war and preparations for future hearings into last year's Bondi terror attack.

Today's hearings focused on the relationship between police and Jewish community security organisations, with Liberal MP Julian Leeser, Dor Foundation chief executive Tahli Blicblau, AFP assistant commissioner Stephen Nutt and Victoria Police assistant commissioner Martin O'Brien among those appearing before the commission.

The evidence is expected to help shape the commission's understanding of police data collection, security risk assessments and the role of emergency preparedness in responding to threats against the Jewish community.

Victoria Police also faced scrutiny over how antisemitic incidents are recorded. The commission heard an abusive phone call to a synagogue, in which the congregation was allegedly described as "genocidal" and "maggot rat Jews", was not recorded as a prejudice-motivated incident.

O'Brien confirmed no incident fact sheet had been logged for the call, which is required for any prejudice-motivated crime that relates to racial, political or ideological circumstances.

O'Brien said the force had "automatic scanning" every day of incidents, along with human analysts to consider threats.

A separate incident involving a 5.5m Nazi hakenkreuz symbol painted on a construction site was also not categorised under the relevant reporting system.

Security funding emerged as one of the dominant themes of the week's hearings, with Jewish community leaders telling the commission families, schools, places of worship and community organisations continue to bear much of the cost of keeping their communities safe.

On Thursday, the commission heard government funding since 2023 has covered about half of the security costs incurred by the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, which received $25 million to distribute to community organisations, places of worship and events.

Executive Council of Australian Jewry co-chief executive Peter Wertheim told the inquiry governments should ideally reimburse the council for all security costs it handles, while almost 200 organisations have applied for the latest federal funding allocation of $124 million over three years.

Driving a BMW, Volpato was allegedly clocked at 109 km/h — nearly 50 km/h over the designated speed limit — when police stopped him on Sydney's Anzac Bridge at 1.10am on Friday.

He was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, police said in a statement.

Volpato had earlier been stopped at 11.05pm on Thursday, police said, for travelling between 86 and 94km/h in a 60 zone.

Volpato returned a negative result when he was given the initial roadside breath test.

Volpato, who plays club football for Italian side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup.

He made headlines shortly before the tournament when he switched his international allegiance from Italy to Australia.

Volpato, who was born and raised in Sydney and played his junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney before moving overseas, represented Italy at U19 and U20 level.

The 22-year-old, who has scored seven goals in his three seasons with Sassuolo after two seasons with fellow Serie A club Roma, said in March he was "waiting for Italy" to select him for the senior side, who subsequently failed to qualify for the World Cup.

title.en: 'We can't stop this virus': Another state records first suspected bird flu case

body.en:
Deadly H5 bird flu appears to have reached Queensland's coastline for the first time as detections in wild seabirds across Australia climb to 17, sparking fresh warnings for vulnerable wildlife.

A deceased petrel found on Moreton Island returned an initial positive result for highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza at the Queensland government's Biosecurity Sciences Laboratory.

Samples have been sent to CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness for confirmatory testing.

Invasive Species Council policy director Carol Booth said the arrival of H5 bird flu in Queensland should alarm anybody concerned about Australia's native animals.

"Bird flu has now reached Queensland's coastline, and that should concern every Australian who cares about our wildlife," Booth said.

"We can't stop this virus, but we can boost the capacity of wildlife to survive and recover from outbreaks."

Australia reported its first case of H5 bird flu on 20 June, and there are now 17 confirmed detections of the serious H5 strain in wild seabirds — 10 in Western Australia, five in South Australia and two in NSW.

Booth said surveillance efforts were working but warned they would not be enough once the virus hit vulnerable species.

"Finding cases is only the first step — once this disease reaches vulnerable wildlife populations, surveillance won't prevent the devastating impacts we've seen overseas," she said.

"Millions of wild birds and marine mammals have died, and unless we do everything we can to strengthen the resilience of at-risk populations, there's every reason to fear Australia could face similar losses."

There have been no detections in poultry and no evidence of large-scale deaths in any animals in Queensland, according to the Department of Primary Industries.

"It is safe to continue to eat chicken meat or eggs, and I would encourage Queenslanders to purchase these products as they normally would," said Queensland's Primary Industries Minister Tony Perrett.

Queensland's Chief Veterinary Officer, Allison Crook, said the suspected positive result was anticipated and the state was well prepared.

"We have known that a H5 bird flu detection in Queensland was a matter of when, not if," Crook said.

"This suspect positive result has not impacted our poultry sector or native wildlife and we are continuing our enhanced passive surveillance program throughout the state and would encourage the community and industry to continue to be vigilant."

Booth continued to urge the federal government to back a major "wildlife resilience" package to help species withstand bird flu and other threats.
